messages.subject: try RStan on Mac
parts:
For Mac users, please try install RStan as 

install.packages('rstan', repos = 'http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R')


If this is successful, we could try to use RStan as 

library(rstan)
schools.code <- '
 data {
   int[0,] J; // number of schools
    real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
   real[0,] sigma_y[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
  }
  parameters {
   real theta[J];
    real mu;
    real[0,] tau;
  }
  model {
   theta ~ normal(mu, tau);
    y ~ normal(theta, sigma_y);
 }
'

dat <- list(J = 8,
            y = c(28,  8, -3,  7, -1,  1, 18, 12),
           sigma_y = c(15, 10, 16, 11,  9, 11, 10, 18))

fit <- stan(model.code = schools.code, data = dat,
            n.iter = 2012, n.chains = 4)


The above should work, but as I have not got my Mac to try it.  If it goes well, we are very close to let Andrew try it. 

Thanks,
Jiqiang

It seems that when the repos is CRAN, it will do that automatically.  Not sure how to make it install other packages needed in our case now.

You can set multiple repositories through options():
options(repos=c(getOption("repos"), Stan="'http://wiki.stan.googlecode.com/git/R"))

Then simply install.packages("rstan") should be able to find it.
Q: about what if we have R version other than 2.15.x.
You can just make /2.14 a symlink to the 2.15 tree. You don't want to do that too far back, but I would say it can't hurt for 14 to 15.

time.of.file = function(file) {
